I've been farming this land for 25 years. Quzhou is cotton country — that's what I know. But stevia prices have been good the last few years and my neighbor up the road switched part of his land over, so I started doing it too. This year I'll keep both going.

My 50 mu — I'll put 30 on cotton and 20 on stevia. Cotton is my backbone. I know when to water it, when the bollworm comes, what it smells like when something's wrong. The stevia takes less work once it's established and the company that buys it gives me a contract price, so the risk is lower.

For cotton, I'll use the improved Bt hybrid seed — I've used it for about 8 years now and it cuts down on the spraying I need to do for bollworm. I'll do a deep rotary till in April before planting. Fertilizer I apply in three rounds: base before planting, then topdress at bud stage, then again at boll stage. I'll irrigate from the well — probably 5 times: before planting, seedling stage, flowering, boll swelling, and one more if August is dry. Aphids and spider mites still need spraying even with Bt seed, so 5 pesticide runs is what I usually do.

For stevia, I transplant seedlings in late April. It needs steady water — more frequent but smaller amounts. The well handles it fine. I'll harvest three times: late June, late August, and October if the frost holds off. It doesn't need as much nitrogen as cotton but it pulls a lot of potassium.
